When VirtueVigil published its first 2026 action ranking in April, 22 films had been reviewed. Two months later the count sits at 31 unique titles. Ten new films have been scored since then, including Mission: Impossible - The Final Reckoning, Beast, The Furious, Brothers Under Fire, Avengers: Doomsday, and Cliffhanger. The updated data changes the picture significantly at both ends of the spectrum.

This ranking covers every 2026 action, superhero, spy, and action-adjacent film scored by VirtueVigil as of June 12, 2026. Films are ordered from most woke (#1) to most traditional (#31). The score margin is the gap between a film's Traditional Values Score and its Woke Score. A positive margin means traditional content outweighed progressive content. A negative margin means the opposite. The original April ranking is archived at Every 2026 Action Movie Ranked (April).

#1 (Most Woke): Supergirl (2026)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: -5 WOKE

Genre: Action / Superhero / Sci-Fi • Woke Score: 12.92 • Trad Score: 8.26

Supergirl takes Tom King's deconstructionist source material and builds a superhero film where heroism is framed as a trauma response rather than a moral choice. The female antihero arc dismantles classical heroism in favor of psychological fragility as the defining character trait, a recurring pattern in DC films adapted from King's work. Three of its top-scoring tropes are explicitly ideological: deconstructed heroine, heroism as trauma, and the Tom King fingerprint that signals the project's philosophical intent before a single frame runs.

#2: The Mandalorian and Grogu (2026)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: -4 WOKE

Genre: Science Fiction / Action / Adventure • Woke Score: 11.4 • Trad Score: 7.8

The Mandalorian and Grogu lands in negative territory despite the franchise's traditionally strong parental-bond storytelling. The theatrical expansion of a streaming series that spent much of its later seasons diluting the original father-surrogate dynamic with ensemble additions and franchise cross-contamination leaves it just below neutral. The core of Mando protecting Grogu is still present but surrounded by enough progressive franchise scaffolding to tip the score.

#3: Deadpool 3 (2026)

MIXED MARGIN: +1 TRAD

Genre: Action / Comedy / Superhero • Woke Score: 9.4 • Trad Score: 10.6

Deadpool 3 is nearly perfectly balanced, which is a feat for a film featuring two of the most chaotic characters in the MCU. Its leading tropes are romantic love as motivating force, loyalty to found family, and heroic violence in service of protection, all traditional frameworks. The crude humor and meta-commentary raise the woke score enough to cancel most of the traditional points. The franchise walks the line it has always walked: traditional values buried under enough irreverence that neither side can claim it.

#4: Over Your Dead Body (2026)

MIXED MARGIN: +1 TRAD

Genre: Comedy / Thriller / Action • Woke Score: 8.64 • Trad Score: 9.18 • Rotten Tomatoes: 71% critics / 68% audience

Over Your Dead Body lands in MIXED territory through a combination of traditional and progressive signals that nearly cancel out. The marital institution is framed as problematic at the plot level, and gender equality in violence is a recurring element. That said, the thriller structure and the moral framework underlying the action sequences keep the traditional score marginally ahead. Barely safe for viewers who prefer content without a lecture, but barely.

#5: One Piece Season 2 (2026)

TRADITIONAL LEAN MARGIN: +4 TRAD

Genre: Action • Woke Score: 3.0 • Trad Score: 7.0

One Piece Season 2 earns a Traditional Lean through the franchise's consistent emphasis on crew loyalty, individual purpose, and the moral clarity of a crew fighting for something larger than themselves. The woke score is low at 3.0, reflecting the source material's mostly apolitical adventure framework. It does not score higher on the traditional side because the season's narrative arcs are not deeply rooted in the traditional values categories that generate high scores.

TRADITIONAL LEAN MARGIN: +5 TRAD

Genre: Action • Woke Score: 1.0 • Trad Score: 6.0

The 2026 Independence Day entry earns a clean Traditional Lean with one of the lowest woke scores on this list at 1.0. #7: Spider-Man: Brand New Day (2026)

TRADITIONAL LEAN MARGIN: +7 TRAD

Genre: Superhero / Action / Adventure • Woke Score: 6.3 • Trad Score: 13.09

Brand New Day's core tropes are self-sacrifice as the highest moral act, continuing duty without recognition, and a mentor figure embodying adult responsibility. Those are among the most traditional frameworks in the superhero genre. The woke score of 6.3 reflects the modern MCU's tendency to insert progressive ensemble elements around its lead, but the film's moral engine is built from the same sacrifice-and-responsibility formula that made No Way Home the most traditionally scored MCU film of its era.

#8: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping (2026)

TRADITIONAL LEAN MARGIN: +7 TRAD

Genre: Dystopian Action • Woke Score: 6.1 • Trad Score: 13.23

Sunrise on the Reaping is a prequel focused on Haymitch Abernathy's first Hunger Games, which means it is structurally required to engage with themes of individual survival against a totalitarian state. The dystopian genre's critique of authoritarian control reads as traditional when the protagonist is an individual resisting state power rather than a collective demanding institutional change. The woke score is contained at 6.1 because the narrative does not route its anti-authoritarianism through identity politics.

#9: Desert Warrior (2026)

TRADITIONAL LEAN MARGIN: +7 TRAD

Genre: Historical Action / Adventure • Woke Score: 7.6 • Trad Score: 14.98 • Rotten Tomatoes: 60% critics / 31% audience

Desert Warrior builds its action framework around a warrior defending female honor against a tyrannical demand, resistance against imperial power, and a strict honor code as the defining character trait. Those are traditional foundations. The significant gap between critic scores (60%) and audience scores (31%) is unusual for a traditional-leaning film and reflects the historical framing generating some critical endorsement while the execution did not satisfy the audience that came for the action.

Beast is a sports-action film built from three foundational traditional tropes: an MMA redemption arc, masculine duty to family as a non-negotiable obligation, and male brotherhood and loyalty. #31 (Most Traditional): The Furious (2026)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL MARGIN: +27 TRAD

Genre: Action / Revenge Thriller / Drama • Woke Score: 1.4 • Trad Score: 28.56 • Rotten Tomatoes: 100% critics • IMDb: 7.7

The Furious is the highest-scoring traditional action film in the 2026 slate at +27 TRAD and the only action film with a 100% critic score on Rotten Tomatoes. Its core tropes are paternal protection as a sacred duty and primary motivation, the father-daughter bond as the emotional core, and male competence and martial skill as heroic virtue. The woke score of 1.4 is near the absolute floor. The Furious makes the case that a father protecting his child is the most morally serious act a man can perform, and it makes that case without apology. With a 100% critic score and a 7.7 on IMDb, the consensus confirms what the VirtueVigil scoring shows: the best action film of 2026 by every meaningful metric.

What the Mid-Year Data Shows

The 2026 action genre has a clear split. The woke end of the spectrum is occupied by IP-driven franchise films: Supergirl and The Mandalorian and Grogu both reflect the ideological direction of their parent studios. The traditional end is dominated by smaller films (Beast, Dhurandhar, Brothers Under Fire, In the Grey) alongside one undisputed mainstream hit (Mission: Impossible - The Final Reckoning) and one critical consensus film (The Furious).

The pattern that has held across every year VirtueVigil has scored holds again in 2026: the highest-scoring traditional films are not the most expensive. They are the ones where the story is not competing with an ideology. Ethan Hunt sacrificing himself. A father hunting down the men who took his daughter. An MMA fighter earning his way back to family. Those stories do not need a budget to work. They need a writer who believes in them.
